mainTopic: Initiating a replacement כהן גדול, the מחלוקת over the כהן הדיוט's אבנט, and the status of the replacement after the original כהן גדול returns.
overview: The amud opens by finishing an earlier question: a replacement כהן גדול needs no special ceremony, because doing the עבודה initiates him, just as later כלים were initiated by their use. Next, רב דימי reports a מחלוקת between רבי and רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון: was a כהן הדיוט's אבנט made of כלאים or of plain linen (בוץ)? The גמרא tries to prove who held which view from a ברייתא, but the proof is rejected because the ברייתא can be read two ways. רבין then brings a clear tradition: everyone agrees about the כהן גדול's אבנט, and רבי says the כהן הדיוט's אבנט is כלאים. רב נחמן בר יצחק supports רבין from a ברייתא in which רבי rejects רבי דוסא's view that the כהן גדול's יום הכפורים garments may be reused by a כהן הדיוט. The גמרא then returns to the replacement כהן גדול. רבי מאיר says the replacement keeps all the laws of a כהן גדול. רבי יוסי says he can serve in neither role, because of איבה and because מעלין בקודש ולא מורידין. The amud ends as רבה בר בר חנה begins a statement in רבי יוחנן's name, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: His service initiates the replacement High Priest
steps.stepSummary: The replacement כהן גדול needs no separate initiation. Doing the עבודה itself initiates him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its final answer to the earlier question of how a substitute כהן גדול gets initiated into his role. The answer is that the act of doing the עבודה is itself the initiation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the גמרא looked for some special act, such as putting on his garments, to initiate the replacement. Here it says no extra step is needed. The very first עבודה he does as כהן גדול makes him the כהן גדול.

keyTerms.meaning: The Temple service
Initiates or inaugurates (from חינוך)
Initiation into use or office

phrases.english: His service initiates him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question on the previous amud: how is the replacement כהן גדול initiated?
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How is a substitute כהן גדול initiated into office?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: His performance of the עבודה initiates him. No separate act is needed.

steps.title: Proof from the vessels משה made
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that משה's כלים were made holy by anointing, but later כלים became holy just by being used. The same is true for the כהן גדול.
steps.simpleTranslation: Wasn't it taught in a ברייתא: all the vessels that משה made were made holy by their anointing. From then on, using them in the service initiates them. Here too, his service initiates him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא supports its answer with a ברייתא about the כלים of the משכן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In משה's time, כלים needed משיחה (anointing with oil). For all later generations, a new כלי became holy simply by being used in the עבודה. The גמרא compares the replacement כהן גדול to these later כלים: his use in the service is his initiation.

keyTerms.meaning: Wasn't it taught? (a formula introducing a supporting ברייתא)
Anointing with the special oil
Makes holy, consecrates
From here onward, in later generations
Here too

phrases.english: Wasn't it taught in a baraita:
all the vessels that Moses made —
their anointing consecrates them;
from then on, their service initiates them.
Here too, his service initiates him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source to support the rule in step 1.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that the replacement כהן גדול is initiated through his עבודה
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: after משה's time, כלים are initiated through their use in the עבודה
steps.whatToRemember: Except for משה's original כלים, holiness comes through use. Using a כלי in the עבודה initiates it, and doing the עבודה initiates a replacement כהן גדול.

steps.title: רב דימי reports a dispute about the ordinary priest's belt
steps.stepSummary: רבי and רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון disagree about the אבנט of a כהן הדיוט. One says it was כלאים, the other says it was בוץ (linen).
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב דימי came, he said: about the belt of an ordinary כהן, רבי and רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון disagree. One said it was made of כלאים (wool and linen). The other said it was made of fine linen.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new topic. רב דימי reports a מחלוקת about the material of an ordinary כהן's אבנט, but he does not say which תנא held which view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה says the כהן גדול's year-round אבנט contained wool and linen (כלאים). The question is whether the כהן הדיוט's אבנט was the same. Since רב דימי leaves the names unmatched, the גמרא will try to work out who said what.

keyTerms.meaning: When רב דימי came (from ארץ ישראל to בבל)
The belt or sash of a כהן
An ordinary כהן, not the כהן גדול
A mixture of wool and linen
Fine linen

phrases.english: When Rav Dimi came, he said:
Regarding the belt of the ordinary priest,
Rabbi and Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon disagree:
one said: it was of diverse kinds (wool and linen);
and one said: it was of fine linen.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new discussion about the אבנט, related to the earlier talk of the כהן גדול's garments.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is a מחלוקת between two named תנאים about whether a כהן הדיוט's אבנט was כלאים or בוץ. The names are not yet matched to the views.
steps.confusionAlert: The phrase "חד אמר... וחד אמר" deliberately does not tell you which רבי said which view. That is exactly what the next steps try to figure out.

steps.title: Suggesting that רבי held the belt was a mixture
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that רבי held the כלאים view. It brings a ברייתא where רבי says the only difference between a כהן גדול and a כהן הדיוט is the אבנט, and רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון says not even the אבנט differs.
steps.simpleTranslation: Conclude that it is רבי who said the belt was כלאים. For a ברייתא teaches: the only difference between a כהן גדול and an ordinary כהן is the belt. These are the words of רבי. רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון says: not even the belt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to match each name to his view by quoting a ברייתא in which the same two תנאים disagree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this ברייתא, רבי says the אבנט differs between the two kinds of כהן, while רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון says even the אבנט is the same. The גמרא will show that if the belts differ, the ordinary כהן's belt must be כלאים. This proof is not finished yet: the גמרא first needs to ask when this ברייתא applies.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it be concluded (introduces a suggested proof)
As it was taught in a ברייתא
The only difference between... is
Not even

phrases.english: Conclude that it is Rabbi
who said it was of diverse kinds.
As it was taught: There is no difference between a High Priest
and an ordinary priest except the belt;
these are the words of Rabbi.
Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon says:
Not even the belt.

steps.triggerLanguage: תִּסְתַּיֵּים דְּרַבִּי הוּא דְּאָמַר שֶׁל כִּלְאַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to resolve the unnamed positions in רב דימי's report.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי is the one who holds that the כהן הדיוט's אבנט was כלאים
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: according to רבי, the only difference between כהן גדול and כהן הדיוט is the אבנט; according to רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, not even that

steps.title: When does the ברייתא apply? Not the rest of the year
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what time of year the ברייתא means. It cannot mean ordinary days, because then the כהן גדול wears eight garments and the כהן הדיוט only four, so there are many differences.
steps.simpleTranslation: When is this? If you say it means the rest of the year, there are many differences: the כהן גדול serves in eight garments and the ordinary כהן in four!
steps.whatsHappening: Before finishing the proof, the גמרא asks what time of year the ברייתא is talking about. It rules out ordinary days. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On a regular day the כהן גדול wears eight בגדים and a כהן הדיוט wears four. So it would be wrong to say that "the only difference" is the אבנט. The ברייתא must be talking about a day when the כהן גדול also wears only four garments.

keyTerms.meaning: When?
If we say
The rest of the days of the year
There are many (differences)

phrases.english: When?
If we say during the rest of the days of the year —
there are many differences:
the High Priest serves in eight garments
and the ordinary priest in four!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵימַת? אִי נֵימָא בִּשְׁאָר יְמוֹת הַשָּׁנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Clarifies the setting of the ברייתא so the proof in step 4 can work.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What time of year does the ברייתא's comparison refer to?
steps.kashyaTarget: Reading the ברייתא as referring to ordinary days
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: On ordinary days the כהן גדול wears eight garments and the כהן הדיוט four. So the אבנט cannot be "the only" difference.

steps.title: Suggesting the ברייתא refers to יום הכפורים
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא must be talking about יום הכפורים, when the כהן גדול also wears four plain linen garments.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, isn't it talking about יום הכפורים?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question: the ברייתא is talking about יום הכפורים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On יום הכפורים the כהן גדול wears four garments of בוץ, including a linen אבנט. Everyone agrees about that. So if רבי says the אבנט still differs, the כהן הדיוט's אבנט must be כלאים, and רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, who says there is no difference, must hold that it is linen. The next step challenges this reading.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, is it not...? (introduces the forced conclusion)
The Day of Atonement, when the כהן גדול serves in four linen garments

phrases.english: Rather, is it not referring to Yom Kippur?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 5 and completes the suggested proof from step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ברייתא refers to יום הכפורים. Therefore רבי, who sees a difference in the אבנט, holds that the כהן הדיוט's אבנט is כלאים.
steps.whyThisMatters: Placing the ברייתא on יום הכפורים is what this proposed proof depends on. Step 7 knocks out exactly this assumption, so the proof does not stand.
steps.whatToRemember: This is only a proposed proof. If the ברייתא refers to יום הכפורים, רבי holds the כהן הדיוט's belt is כלאים. But step 7 rejects this reading, and only רבין's report in step 8 settles who holds what.

steps.title: Rejecting the proof: the ברייתא means ordinary days and only the shared garments
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the יום הכפורים reading. The ברייתא can mean ordinary days, comparing only the four garments both כהנים wear. That flips who holds what, so there is no proof that רבי says כלאים for the כהן הדיוט.
steps.simpleTranslation: They answer: No. Really the ברייתא is talking about the rest of the year, and only about the garments that are the same for both כהנים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof from Steps 4-6. It offers another way to read the ברייתא, so the proof falls apart.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 5 said 'ordinary days' could not work because the כהן גדול has eight garments and the כהן הדיוט has four. The answer is that the ברייתא compares only the four garments both of them wear, and among those the only possible difference is the אבנט. On ordinary days the כהן גדול's אבנט is כלאים. So רבי, who says 'the אבנט differs,' holds that the כהן הדיוט's is linen. רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, who says 'not even the אבנט differs,' holds that it is כלאים, which is the opposite of what Step 4 assumed.

keyTerms.meaning: 'They say.' This introduces an answer from the scholars of the בית מדרש, often a rejection.
'Really' or 'actually.' It introduces the true reading after a rejected one.
The rest of the year, meaning ordinary days that are not יום הכפורים.
'Those that are equal.' Here it means the four garments both כהנים wear.

steps.confusionAlert: Under this new reading the two opinions switch places. Here רבי says the כהן הדיוט's אבנט is linen, which is the reverse of what Step 4 tried to prove.

phrases.english: They say: No,
really, it refers to the rest of the days of the year,
and only to those garments that are common to both.
phrases.notes: The four garments: tunic, trousers, turban, and belt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof by reopening the 'ordinary days' reading that Step 5 had ruled out.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole proof that רבי holds the כהן הדיוט's אבנט is כלאים.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the ברייתא must mean יום הכפורים. It can mean ordinary days if it compares only the shared garments, and then the opinions are reversed.

steps.title: רבין's clear version of where they agree and where they argue
steps.stepSummary: רבין reports that everyone agrees the כהן גדול's אבנט is linen on יום הכפורים and כלאים the rest of the year. The only dispute is the כהן הדיוט's אבנט, all year round: רבי says כלאים, and רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון says linen.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבין came, he said: Everyone agrees the כהן גדול's belt on יום הכפורים is linen. Everyone agrees it is כלאים the rest of the year. They argued only about the belt of a regular כהן, both during the year and on יום הכפורים. רבי says it is כלאים, and רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון says it is linen.
steps.whatsHappening: רבין arrives from ארץ ישראל with a tradition that settles who holds what. It confirms the original idea that רבי says כלאים for the כהן הדיוט.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבין first removes the כהן גדול from the debate, since everyone agrees about him. That leaves one question: what is the כהן הדיוט's אבנט made of? According to רבין, רבי holds כלאים and רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון holds plain linen, and this does not change on יום הכפורים.

keyTerms.meaning: 'When רבין came' from ארץ ישראל to בבל, bringing a tradition.
Everyone agrees.
They argued only about the following.
Fine linen.

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבין, the only argument is about the כהן הדיוט's אבנט. רבי says כלאים, and רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון says linen.

phrases.english: When Ravin came, he said:

phrases.aramaic: אַבְנֵטוֹ שֶׁל כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל בְּיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים —
phrases.english: The belt of the High Priest on Yom Kippur —
everyone agrees it is of linen.
During the rest of the days of the year —
everyone agrees it is of mixed wool and linen.
They disagreed only
about the belt of the regular priest,

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין בִּשְׁאָר יְמוֹת הַשָּׁנָה, בֵּין בְּיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים.
phrases.english: both during the rest of the year and on Yom Kippur.
For Rabbi says: It is of mixed wool and linen,

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: שֶׁל בּוּץ.
phrases.english: and Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon says: It is of linen.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After Step 7 left it unclear who holds what, רבין gives a clear tradition that matches the original assumption.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Everyone agrees about the כהן גדול's אבנט. On the כהן הדיוט's אבנט, all year round, רבי says כלאים and רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון says בוץ.

steps.title: רב נחמן בר יצחק brings a supporting ברייתא: רבי יהודה's reading of the extra word
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק says a ברייתא supports רבין. It asks why the פסוק about removing the ashes adds the word 'ילבש'. רבי יהודה answers that it teaches the כהן also wears the turban and belt for this service.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: We also learned this in a ברייתא. Since the פסוק says 'upon his flesh,' why does it need to say 'he shall wear'? To include the turban and the belt for removing the ashes. These are the words of רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a proof for רבין's version. This step sets up the ברייתא by quoting the first opinion in it, and the key part comes in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא learns something from an extra word in the פסוק about תרומת הדשן (removing the ashes). רבי יהודה uses the word to teach that the turban and belt are worn for this service too. His opinion is background; the part that proves רבין's point is still coming.

keyTerms.meaning: 'We too have learned it.' This introduces a source that supports the previous statement.
'Why does the verse say?' It points to a word that seems extra.
'To include.' It shows what the extra word adds.
Removing the ashes from the מזבח each morning.
The turban worn by a כהן.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
We too have learned this in a baraita:
"Upon his flesh" — why does the verse say "he shall wear"?
phrases.notes: ויקרא ו:ג. The word 'wear' seems extra.

phrases.english: To include the turban and the belt
for the removal of the ashes,
these are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a proof from a ברייתא to support רבין's version in Step 8.
steps.raayaObject: רבין's report that רבי holds the כהן הדיוט's אבנט is כלאים.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא on ויקרא ו:ג containing a disagreement among רבי יהודה, רבי דוסא, and רבי.

steps.title: רבי דוסא: the כהן גדול's יום הכפורים clothes may be used by a regular כהן
steps.stepSummary: רבי דוסא reads the extra word differently. It teaches that the four linen garments the כהן גדול wore on יום הכפורים may later be worn by a כהן הדיוט.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי דוסא says: The word comes to include the clothes of the כהן גדול from יום הכפורים, teaching that they are fit for a regular כהן to wear.
steps.whatsHappening: Still inside the ברייתא, a second תנא gives another use for the extra word. This sets up the opinion that רבי will reject in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי דוסא assumes the כהן גדול's יום הכפורים garments match what a כהן הדיוט wears, so a regular כהן can reuse them. That only works if the belts are the same, which means the כהן הדיוט's belt would be linen. רבי's rejection of this is what proves the point.

keyTerms.meaning: The four white linen garments the כהן גדול wears on יום הכפורים.
Fit or valid for use.

phrases.english: Rabbi Dosa says:

phrases.aramaic: לְהָבִיא בִּגְדֵי כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל בְּיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים,
phrases.english: It comes to include the garments of the High Priest on Yom Kippur,
that they are fit for a regular priest.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second opinion within the same ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The יום הכפורים garments of the כהן גדול may afterward be worn by a כהן הדיוט.

steps.title: רבי's first objection: the belts are not the same
steps.stepSummary: רבי gives two objections to רבי דוסא. The first is that the כהן גדול's יום הכפורים belt is not the same as a regular כהן's belt. This shows that for רבי the כהן הדיוט's belt is כלאים, which supports רבין.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי says: There are two answers against this. First: the belt of the כהן גדול on יום הכפורים is not the same as the belt of a regular כהן.
steps.whatsHappening: Inside the ברייתא, רבי attacks רבי דוסא's view. This is the line that proves רב נחמן בר יצחק's point. The second objection comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The כהן גדול's יום הכפורים belt is linen, and רבי says it is different from the כהן הדיוט's belt. So for רבי the כהן הדיוט's belt must be כלאים. This is exactly what רבין reported in Step 8.

keyTerms.meaning: 'There are two objections to this,' meaning two reasons to reject the view.
'One,' meaning the first of the objections.

steps.whyThisMatters: This line is the actual proof for רבין's version. רבי openly says the יום הכפורים linen belt differs from the regular כהן's belt, so he must hold that the regular כהן's belt is כלאים.

phrases.english: Rabbi says:
There are two objections to this matter.
One:

phrases.aramaic: דְּאַבְנֵטוֹ שֶׁל כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל בְּיוֹם הַכִּיפּוּרִים
phrases.english: that the belt of the High Priest on Yom Kippur

phrases.aramaic: לֹא זֶה הוּא אַבְנֵטוֹ שֶׁל כֹּהֵן הֶדְיוֹט.
phrases.english: is not the same as the belt of a regular priest.
phrases.notes: So for רבי, the כהן הדיוט's belt is כלאים.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי rejects רבי דוסא's view from Step 10, and that rejection completes the proof for Step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי דוסא's claim that the כהן גדול's יום הכפורים garments are fit for a כהן הדיוט.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The garments cannot be reused by a כהן הדיוט, because his belt is different (כלאים) from the כהן גדול's linen יום הכפורים belt.

steps.title: Holy clothes cannot go down to a lesser use
steps.stepSummary: רבי's second objection to רבי דוסא: garments used for the holiest service should not later be used for a lesser service.
steps.simpleTranslation: And another point: garments that were used for a very high level of holiness, should they then be used for a lower level of holiness?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי gives a second reason why רבי דוסא must be wrong. The clothes from the כהן גדול's יום הכפורים service should not be passed down to a regular כהן for ordinary work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי דוסא said a כהן הדיוט may later wear the כהן גדול's יום הכפורים linen garments. רבי objects with a basic rule of holiness: you do not take something from a higher holy use and lower it to a lesser use. The יום הכפורים service inside the קודש הקדשים is the highest level of holiness, so those clothes cannot be 'downgraded.'

keyTerms.meaning: And furthermore. Introduces an additional objection.
A severe, higher level of holiness (here, the יום הכפורים service)
A lighter, lower level of holiness (here, a regular כהן's service)

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the principle of מעלין בקודש ולא מורידין: holiness only goes up, never down. The same idea comes back later on this amud in רבי יוסי's view about the replacement כהן גדול (steps 16–18).

phrases.aramaic: וְעוֹד: בְּגָדִים שֶׁנִּשְׁתַּמַּשְׁתָּה בָּהֶן קְדוּשָּׁה חֲמוּרָה,
phrases.english: And furthermore: garments with which a severe holiness was served,
phrases.notes: The garments of the כהן גדול on יום הכפורים

phrases.english: should a light holiness be served with them?
phrases.notes: A rhetorical question: of course not

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעוֹד: בְּגָדִים שֶׁנִּשְׁתַּמַּשְׁתָּה בָּהֶן קְדוּשָּׁה חֲמוּרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This is the second of רבי's two objections. The first one was in step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי דוסא's reading that a כהן הדיוט may wear the כהן גדול's יום הכפורים garments
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Holy items may not be lowered from a higher holiness to a lower one. So clothes from the יום הכפורים service cannot be used for ordinary service.

steps.title: רבי's own reading: even worn-out garments are allowed
steps.stepSummary: רבי explains the extra word 'ילבש' differently. It teaches that worn, threadbare garments may still be used.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, what does the word 'he shall put on' come to teach? It comes to include worn-out garments.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי has rejected רבי דוסא's explanation. Now he gives his own explanation of why the פסוק says 'ילבש.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each opinion has to explain the extra word somehow. For רבי, it teaches that a כהן may wear old, threadbare garments, as long as they are not torn apart. So the extra word teaches something real, without needing רבי דוסא's idea of passing clothes down.

keyTerms.meaning: What does the verse come to teach? Asks why an extra word was written.
To include (something extra)
Worn-out, threadbare garments

phrases.english: Rather, what does the verse teach by saying 'shall put on'?
phrases.notes: רבי asks this according to his own view

phrases.english: To include the worn-out garments.
phrases.notes: They are valid for service as long as they are not completely ripped

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting רבי דוסא, רבי offers a different use for the extra word.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the extra word 'ילבש' teaches, if not רבי דוסא's idea
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It includes worn-out (שחקין) garments as valid for service.

steps.title: רבי דוסא is consistent: the garments do not need to be hidden away
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that רבי דוסא's view matches his opinion in another ברייתא. There he holds that the יום הכפורים garments do not need גניזה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי דוסא follows his own reasoning. As it was taught: 'and he shall leave them there' teaches that the garments must be hidden away. רבי דוסא says: it only means he may not use them on another יום הכפורים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that רבי דוסא is being consistent with himself. In another ברייתא he also holds that the יום הכפורים garments may be used again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The anonymous view reads 'והניחם שם' to mean the garments must be put away forever (גניזה). רבי דוסא says it only bans the כהן גדול from wearing them on a future יום הכפורים. This leaves room for a כהן הדיוט to use them, which fits what he said in step 10.

keyTerms.meaning: He follows his own reasoning (he is consistent with what he says elsewhere)
'And he shall leave them there' (ויקרא טז:כג)
They must be stored away and never used again

steps.confusionAlert: 'Another יום הכפורים' does not mean another person wearing them on יום הכפורים. It means the same garments may not be used for the יום הכפורים service in a later year. For other uses, רבי דוסא allows them.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Dosa follows his own reasoning,
as it was taught: 'and he shall leave them there,'
teaches that they require being hidden away.
Rabbi Dosa says:
that he should not use them
on another Yom Kippur.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the discussion of רבי דוסא by linking his view to another ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי דוסא really holds the יום הכפורים garments can be reused by a כהן הדיוט
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא on 'והניחם שם', where רבי דוסא says the garments do not need גניזה

steps.title: רבי מאיר: the replacement keeps all the laws of a כהן גדול
steps.stepSummary: New topic: a substitute כהן גדול. רבי מאיר says the original returns to his job, and the substitute keeps all the laws of a כהן גדול.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: If something made the כהן גדול unfit and they appointed another in his place, the first one goes back to his service. The second one has all the מצוות of the כהן גדול upon him. These are the words of רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to its earlier topic: appointing a backup כהן גדול. It quotes a ברייתא about what happens to the backup after the original כהן גדול becomes fit again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Say the כהן גדול becomes unfit (for example, he became טמא), and someone else replaces him. When the original becomes fit again, he goes back to his role. רבי מאיר says the replacement does not lose his status. He wears the eight garments and keeps all the special rules of a כהן גדול, such as not marrying a widow and not becoming טמא for relatives.

keyTerms.meaning: Something happened that made him unfit to serve
They appointed someone else in his place
The office of כהן גדול

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: If a disqualification befell him
and they appointed another in his place,
the first one returns to his service,

phrases.aramaic: שֵׁנִי — כׇּל מִצְוֹת כְּהוּנָּה גְּדוֹלָה עָלָיו,
phrases.english: the second one: all the מצוות of the High Priesthood are upon him,
phrases.notes: Eight garments, the marriage rules, the rules about טומאה

phrases.english: these are the words of Rabbi Meir.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אֵירַע בּוֹ פְּסוּל וּמִינּוּ אַחֵר תַּחְתָּיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא leaves the belt and garments discussion and returns to the topic of the substitute כהן גדול.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The original כהן גדול goes back to his service. The replacement keeps all the laws of a כהן גדול.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: the replacement fits neither role
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי agrees that the original goes back. But he says the replacement may now serve neither as כהן גדול nor as a regular כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי says: The first one goes back to his service. The second one is not fit to serve as a כהן גדול, and not as a regular כהן.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי argues with רבי מאיר about the replacement. He says the replacement is stuck: he cannot serve in either role.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He cannot serve as כהן גדול, because there is already a כהן גדול and two would cause friction. He also cannot go back to being a כהן הדיוט with four garments, because once raised to higher holiness he cannot be lowered. This is the same idea as step 12: holiness goes up, not down.

keyTerms.meaning: He is not fit to serve
A regular כהן who wears four garments

steps.whatToRemember: רבי מאיר: the replacement keeps full כהן גדול status. רבי יוסי: the replacement may serve as neither, because he cannot share the top role and cannot be lowered.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says:
the first one returns to his service,
phrases.notes: Same as רבי מאיר on this point

phrases.english: the second one is not fit

phrases.aramaic: לֹא לְכֹהֵן גָּדוֹל, וְלֹא לְכֹהֵן הֶדְיוֹט,
phrases.english: neither as a High Priest, nor as a common priest,
phrases.notes: Not as כהן גדול because of two כהנים גדולים; not as הדיוט because holiness is not lowered

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: רִאשׁוֹן חוֹזֵר לַעֲבוֹדָתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This is the opposing opinion in the same ברייתא, disagreeing with רבי מאיר about the replacement.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The replacement may serve neither as כהן גדול nor as a כהן הדיוט.

steps.title: רבי יוסי brings a story to prove his view
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי supports his view with a real event involving יוסף בן אלם. There the חכמים ruled that the replacement could serve neither as כהן גדול nor as a regular כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי said: There was a story with יוסף בן אלם from ציפורי. The כהן גדול became disqualified, and they appointed יוסף in his place. The חכמים said: The first one goes back to his service. The second one is not fit to be a כהן גדול or a regular כהן.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי is not just stating his opinion again. He is pointing to a real case where the חכמים ruled exactly the way he holds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 16, רבי יוסי said the replacement can serve in neither role. Now he shows this was an actual ruling of the חכמים in a real case. He brings it as support against רבי מאיר, who said the replacement keeps all the laws of a כהן גדול.

keyTerms.meaning: A story or real event, often brought as proof for a הלכה
The כהן who was appointed as the substitute כהן גדול
ציפורי, a city in the גליל
A disqualification; something that made the כהן גדול unable to serve
They appointed him in his place
A regular, ordinary כהן, not the כהן גדול

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think יוסף בן אלם was the one who became disqualified. The disqualification happened to the כהן גדול. יוסף בן אלם was the replacement, the 'second one' in the ruling.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei said:
There was an incident with Yosef ben Elem of Tzippori
in which a disqualification happened to the High Priest
phrases.notes: The disqualification was the כהן גדול's, not יוסף's.

phrases.english: and they appointed him (Yosef) in his place,
and the Sages said:
The first one returns to his service,
the second one is not fit

phrases.aramaic: לֹא לְכֹהֵן גָּדוֹל, וְלֹא לְכֹהֵן הֶדְיוֹט.
phrases.english: neither to be High Priest nor to be a common priest.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי: מַעֲשֶׂה בְּיוֹסֵף בֶּן אִלֵּם בְּצִיפּוֹרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי יוסי's ruling from Step 16 with a real case decided by the חכמים.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוסי's view that the original כהן גדול returns and the substitute may serve in neither role.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The real case of יוסף בן אלם in ציפורי, where the חכמים ruled this way.

steps.title: Why the replacement cannot serve in either role
steps.stepSummary: The replacement cannot be כהן גדול because of jealousy and bad feelings. He cannot go back to being a regular כהן because in holy matters we raise people up and do not bring them down.
steps.simpleTranslation: He cannot be כהן גדול, because of bad feelings. He cannot be a regular כהן, because in holy matters we go up, not down.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the reason behind each half of the ruling: why not כהן גדול, and why not a regular כהן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two separate reasons. Having two equal כהנים גדולים at the same time would cause jealousy and resentment (איבה). Sending him back down to a regular כהן would break the rule that holiness only goes up (מעלין בקודש ולא מורידין). Together, these reasons leave him stuck in between, with no role.

keyTerms.meaning: Hatred, jealousy, or bad feelings between people
Because of; introduces a reason
We raise up in matters of holiness
And we do not bring down

steps.whatToRemember: The replacement is stuck. He cannot be כהן גדול because of איבה, and he cannot go back to being a regular כהן because of מעלין בקודש ולא מורידין.
steps.whyThisMatters: The rule מעלין בקודש ולא מורידין is a general principle. It appears in many places across ש"ס, not just here.

phrases.english: Not as High Priest, because of hatred.
phrases.notes: Two equal כהנים גדולים would lead to jealousy.

phrases.english: Not as a common priest, because we elevate in holiness
and we do not downgrade.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasons behind the חכמים' two-part ruling in Step 17.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The substitute cannot be כהן גדול because of איבה. He cannot be a regular כהן because of מעלין בקודש ולא מורידין.

steps.title: Opening of a new statement by רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר בר חנה begins reporting something he heard from רבי יוחנן. The content of the statement comes in the next section.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה said that רבי יוחנן said:
steps.whatsHappening: This line only tells us who is speaking. The actual statement continues in the next part of the text, so the גמרא is setting up its next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a chain of transmission: רבה בר בר חנה is quoting his teacher רבי יוחנן. We will only know the content and purpose of the statement in the next section. It appears here because this passage ends at this point.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who often reports teachings of רבי יוחנן
A leading אמורא of ארץ ישראל
'Said that X said': a formula for quoting a teaching in someone else's name

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Chana said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
phrases.notes: Attribution only. The statement itself continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attribution line that opens a new statement, which continues in the next section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Not yet stated. The content follows on the next amud.
